temp_level.name: earth_temp_level

support_gate.definition: achieved weight total over expected weight total: the cos(lat)-weighted fraction of the native cells falling in the pixel that carried a usable value
support_gate.thin_support_warning: A pixel passing the coverage gate on a small support fraction is a weak measurement, not a missing one. Filter on support, not on validity alone.

temp_level.record: calendar 2025 only, 12 months, Terra AND Aqua
temp_level.diurnal_definition: max minus min over the AVAILABLE LOCAL TIMES -- the SAME quantity the Moon and Mars carry. Sample counts: Earth 4, Mars 12, Moon 96. This replaces the earlier two-sample Terra day-minus-night, which was a different physical quantity and could go negative; max minus min cannot, by construction.
temp_level.overpass_times: Terra ~10:30/22:30, Aqua ~13:30/01:30 local. These are MISSION DESIGN. The products' own view-time fields do not reproduce them when read: the distributions come out near-uniform over 0-24 h and Terra 'night' lands at 14.4 h. Two hypotheses were tested and REJECTED -- a 0.1 scale factor (caps at 12 h, cannot hold a night overpass) and swapped day/night bands (gives 14.4/9.0, still wrong). The times are therefore not claimed as measured, and nothing here depends on them: four distinct samples is all max-minus-min needs.
temp_level.cross_platform: Terra and Aqua are different instruments with independent calibration drift. For a rank transform computed WITHIN Earth this is negligible, because a common offset cannot change an ordering. Stated rather than assumed away.
temp_level.record_cost: ONE calendar year. A single anomalous season -- an El Nino, a volcanic aerosol loading, an unusual monsoon -- is not averaged out at all. The 22-month Terra record was longer, but the platforms did not line up, and consistency was the defect worth fixing.
temp_level.coverage_note: MOD11C3 and MYD11C3 are LAND ONLY and gap in polar night, so coverage varies by month. n_months is carried as the support value.
temp_level.resampling_note: BIN THEN FILL. Pixels whose footprint contained at least one source cell carry an area-weighted MEAN of those cells. Pixels with no source cell carry a nearest-neighbour COPY and are marked by SUPPORT EXACTLY 0.0 ALONGSIDE A FINITE VALUE -- that combination means copied, not missing. A plate carree source is not uniformly coarse: a 0.5 degree cell is 15.2 km north-south but 15.2*cos(lat) km east-west, so the same source is finer than the pixel near the poles and coarser near the equator. Copying everywhere would have thrown away real polar detail in the lunar target region; binning everywhere would have left most of the sphere empty, which the coverage gate caught at 28.88% valid.
temp_level.tie_note: distinct_levels and largest_tie_fraction are the FOURTH gate. Copied pixels make neighbours carry identical values, and range, coverage and support are all blind to that.

sampling_support.definition: n_months (earth) or n_local_time bins (moon); stored as <body>_thermal_nsamples
